output.title: Design against vendor price changes with one simple control
output.body:
When a vendor changes price, the real question is not “is this annoying?” It is: does this cost sit inside a repeatable workflow that you can actually measure and replace if needed?

For a small business, I would keep this simple. Pick one workflow that already depends on a vendor tool — invoicing, customer reply triage, or manual data entry. Then write down three things: the current per-use or per-user cost, what event would trigger a review, and whether that step could be swapped out without breaking the rest of the process.

That gives you a bounded decision instead of a vague worry. If the vendor cost rises and the workflow is low-frequency, maybe you keep it. If the same tool sits inside a high-frequency process and the price change would push you toward more manual work or delay a hire, the pressure is different.

One practical next step: make a quarterly vendor-cost check for that single workflow. Note the current rate, any change notice, and the point where you would revisit the setup. Keep the final approval human. No heroics, just a better grip on the boring part of the stack.
